title: Risotto ai Funghi Misti
subtitle: risotto with a mix of fresh and dried mushrooms
excerpt: Risotto ai funghi misti uses a combination of fresh chestnut mushrooms, oyster mushrooms, and dried porcini to build a risotto with layered mushroom flavour. Each variety contributes something different. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Risotto with mixed mushrooms is a standard of northern Italian home cooking, particularly in Lombardy, Veneto, and Piedmont. The funghi misti approach, using several mushroom varieties together, produces a more complex result than any single mushroom alone. Pellegrino Artusi, La scienza in cucina (1891, public domain in Italy), documents mushroom-based risotti as central dishes of northern Italian cuisine. The combination of dried porcini (for depth) with fresh cultivated mushrooms (for texture) is a practical technique for year-round cooking.

glossaryTerms.definition: Mixed mushrooms, using at least two varieties for complexity. In this risotto: chestnut mushrooms for bulk and texture, oyster mushrooms for their delicate flavour, and dried porcini soaked in hot water to provide deep earthy stock and intensity.

content.text: works better than a single-mushroom risotto because the varieties support each other. Dried porcini soaked in hot water create an earthy, intense liquid that becomes part of the stock. Fresh chestnut mushrooms, browned in butter before the rice is added, provide sweet, firm texture. Oyster mushrooms, added at the end, contribute a delicate, silky character that would be lost if added earlier.

The method follows the standard risotto approach: soffritto, toast the rice, wine, then stock ladle by ladle. The mantecatura at the end with cold butter and Parmesan is not optional; it is what makes the difference between a satisfying bowl and a great one.

items.prepNote: soaked in 300 ml hot water 20 minutes, drained, liquid strained

content.text: Soak {{mushrooms-porcini-dried}} of dried porcini in 300 ml of hot water for 20 minutes. Lift out, chop roughly, and strain the liquid. Add the liquid to {{stock-vegetable}} of hot vegetable stock in a saucepan. Keep warm.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in the risotto pan over high heat. Add {{mushrooms-chestnut}} of chestnut mushrooms and cook without stirring for 2 to 3 minutes until browned. Stir and cook 2 minutes more. Remove and set aside.

In the same pan over medium heat, add the remaining olive oil. Cook {{onion}} of onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and cook 1 minute. Add the chopped porcini and the browned chestnut mushrooms back to the pan.

Add {{arborio-rice}} of risotto rice and toast for 1 minute, stirring. Add {{dry-white-wine}} of wine and stir until absorbed. Add the warm mushroom stock a ladle at a time, stirring and waiting for each addition to absorb before adding the next. This takes 18 to 20 minutes.

When the rice is cooked through but still has slight bite, add {{mushrooms-oyster}} of oyster mushrooms and stir for 1 minute. Take off the heat. Stir in {{unsalted-butter}} of cold butter and {{parmesan}} of Parmesan vigorously for 2 minutes. Season. Rest 1 minute and serve in warm bowls.

items.symptom: Risotto lacks depth of mushroom flavour
items.cause: Porcini soaking liquid discarded, or chestnut mushrooms not properly browned
items.fix: Always use the strained porcini liquid as part of the stock. Brown the mushrooms hard before starting the risotto base.

items.symptom: Oyster mushrooms are tough and rubbery
items.fix: Add oyster mushrooms only in the final minute. They need almost no cooking; residual heat is sufficient.

content.text: Mixed mushroom risotto is autumn home cooking from northern Italy. The mushroom mix changes with what is available. The combination here works year-round with shop-bought mushrooms. In autumn, use chanterelles or fresh ceps instead of oyster mushrooms when you can get them. The dried porcini matter in all seasons. Without them the risotto is good but lacks the depth that makes this one of the benchmarks of Italian cooking.
